transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 14:30 UTC | Duration 45m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Lara (Lattice Head of ML), Samir (Infra), Jon (CTO)

Auto-summary: short discovery on latency/throughput needs for real-time fraud detection and transaction enrichment. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) deployments, wants p95 <150ms for short prompts and token/sec targets for batch scoring. Agreed to run token/sec benchmarks and share prompts.

Topics: p95 latency targets, concurrency (qps), streaming vs non-streaming, token/sec benchmarking, KV/prefix caching, security/compliance (SOC2, KMS), pricing next steps.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um i'm maya from Redwood, and daniel our systems engineer is with me. can you do a quick intro?
[00:08] Lara: sure, i'm lara head of ml at lattice, we run transaction risk models and realtime enrichment, looking at adding llm features for explanation generation and anomaly summarization.
[00:15] Jon: jon, cto, i'll be listening for infra constraints and compliance needs.
[00:19] Samir: samir infra, i'll handle networking and capacity questions.
[00:23] Maya: great, quick agenda: we want to understand your latency p95 goals, typical concurrency, whether streaming is required, and which deployment mode you're leaning toward. then we'll propose a benchmark plan. sound ok?
[00:33] Lara: yep that's perfect. our hard constraint is p95 under 150ms for short inference (like 40-80 tokens) for the UI snippets, and for async batch scoring we need high tokens/sec -- around 500k tokens/sec aggregate during nightly jobs.
[00:46] Daniel: ok that helps. are the 150ms requests single-turn prompts? do you need streaming or is non-streamed response okay?
[00:53] Lara: mostly single-turn, a few multi-turn but short contexts. we want streaming for the UI so responses feel instant, but p95 for the first token is most critical.
[01:02] Maya: understood. and concurrency—what's peak qps for the UI path?
[01:06] Lara: peak about 120 concurrent users, bursts to 250. average qps ~80.
[01:11] Samir: on infra we prefer VPC/private deployment for data residency and audit, but open to dedicated hosted if it meets SOC2 + KMS requirements.
[01:20] Daniel: that's common. for p95 150ms on 40-80 tokens with streaming, two levers matter: model selection/quantization and locality (region/GPU type). can you share whether you need open models or vendor models?
[01:31] Lara: open models preferred for cost, but quality must hit our accuracy thresholds. we've tried some 7b quantized models and p95 was ok on single GPU but burst concurrency killed latency.
[01:43] Daniel: yep, burst concurrency often causes scheduling queuing. Redwood Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable latency since we provision concurrency capacity. Hosted has autoscaling but can do cold-starts depending on warm pools.
[01:56] Jon: can you explain the warm pool behavior and cold start impact? we can't have page load stalls for customers.
[02:02] Daniel: sure, in hosted we keep model instances in warm pools; if burst exceeds warm capacity, new instances spin up which adds tens to hundreds ms depending on model size and quantization. Dedicated lets you reserve GPU slots so you don't hit that. we also do prefix/KV cache so repeated prefixes are instant once cached.
[02:19] Lara: how does kv cache handle multi-tenant workloads? we worry about data mixing and eviction.
[02:24] Daniel: cache is tenant-isolated. eviction policies can be tuned per tenant, and caching is disabled for workloads that require strict data isolation. for private deployment we can deploy within your VPC and use customer-managed KMS for keys.
[02:36] Samir: what about p95 measurement—do you report first-token p95 and overall response-time p95?
[02:41] Maya: yes we can surface both: first-byte/first-token latency, and end-to-end completion latency, plus per-route token cost and token/sec metrics. we usually run benchmarks to report p50/p95/p99 across sample prompts.
[02:52] Lara: good. for batch scoring, we need token/sec baseline. could you walk through how you'd benchmark tokens/sec?
[02:58] Daniel: sure. we run synthetic and representative prompt sets. for throughput benchmarks we use large batches on dedicated instances, measure steady-state tokens/sec, and include GPU utilization, memory, and tail latency. we'll give you a script that runs sequences at different batch sizes and concurrency to map tradeoffs.
[03:15] Jon: what's a realistic tokens/sec for a single A100-equivalent GPU for a 7b quantized model?
[03:21] Daniel: ballpark numbers: optimized runtime can do 150-300k tokens/sec single stream for 7b on A100 when batched well; for 13b it's lower, maybe 60-120k tokens/sec depending on sequence length and quantization. these numbers vary a lot by kernel, batch, and prompt length.
[03:36] Lara: our nightly pipeline needs 500k tokens/sec aggregate; we'd run on a cluster of GPUs. what's the best way to size?
[03:43] Daniel: we'll take your prompt distribution and simulate. often customers start with dedicated pool of N GPUs and use autoscale for burst. with 7b at 200k each, you'd need ~3 GPUs steady; include headroom for failures and can size to 4-5 for bursts.
[03:56] Samir: and pricing—how does dedicated pricing compare to hosted per-token? we need a TCO comparison.
[04:02] Maya: we'll send a dedicated vs hosted TCO spreadsheet. dedicated is reserved capacity (monthly commit) so unit cost lower at scale; hosted is usage-based and simpler for short pilots.
[04:11] Lara: ok, also we have strict compliance: SOC2, SSO, audit logs, customer-managed KMS, and data residency in eu-west-1. can you do that in hosted?
[04:20] Daniel: hosted supports SOC2 and SAML SSO, but for customer-managed KMS and strict VPC-only egress, Private deployment or Dedicated in a VPC is the right fit. we support bringing your own KMS and on-prem connectors for private installs.
[04:33] Jon: if we choose private deployment, what's the deployment footprint and ops burden?
[04:37] Daniel: private has a customer-managed control plane overlay; we provide a deployment package and ops runbook. typical footprint for our private stack is a few control-plane VMs plus GPUs; we work with your infra team for network setup. ops burden is higher than hosted but we provide an enterprise support package.
[04:51] Lara: any known gotchas with streaming and p95? we've seen models that stream slowly and increase tail latency.
[04:57] Daniel: yeah streaming increases complexity because first-token latency is critical; you need small generation steps and efficient kernel paths. our runtime optimizes for small-step streaming and does micro-batching for throughput while preserving first-token latency. we'll validate with your prompts.
[05:12] Samir: for the benchmark script, will it include region-aware routing and simulated warm caches?
[05:16] Daniel: yes we'll include warm-cache runs, cold-start runs, and simulated regional routing to estimate cross-region latencies.
[05:24] Maya: next steps recap: daniel will share benchmark scripts and infra checklist; lara will share prompt set and target SLO doc; maya will send dedicated vs hosted tco. schedule follow-up in a week to review results.
[05:36] Lara: sounds good. quick Q — do you have any existing customers with similar real-time requirements?
[05:40] Maya: yes, we have customers in payments and retail with p95 100-200ms targets using dedicated pools, we can anonymize benchmarks.
[05:48] Jon: ok thanks, i'm comfortable with a pilot if bench results look good.
[05:52] Maya: great we'll get things moving. thanks everyone.

Meeting end.
